sections.html: Phractolaemus are air breathers. It is said that these fish can attain a maximum length of about 20 cm. The photographed male, which clearly shows breeding tubercles, is about 8 cm long.
Formerly these fish were obtained from Nigeria; this time they originate from the Congo.

Sexually active males develop breeding tubercles along the flanks and around the eyes.

In the current import two colour morphs appear, a more reddish one and a more blackish one. Such differences were not observed in former importations; the Nigerian fish were uniformly brownish.

These unique fishes are said to be close relatives of the Kneriidae on the one side, but they also show many relations to the bony tongues, and here especially to the butterfly fish, Pantodon buchholzi. There is almost nothing known on the natural history of these unusual fishes.
